guide.summary: Own OAuth app, unpublished, customer admins enable (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)); Listed in Box Integrations (app review); Technology Partner Program (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Easiest: Own OAuth app, unpublished, customer admins enable (self-serve (no review step found in the docs)). Hardest: Listed in Box Integrations (app review).

composio.note: Composio has a managed OAuth app for Box, which is enough for prototypes. The separate Box MCP toolkit is not managed and needs your own OAuth app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Box app. For launch you likely want your own app so the consent screen shows your brand and you get a dedicated quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Dedicated rate-limit quota instead of one shared across Composio users
Custom scopes, polling intervals or rate limits
Required if you use the separate Box MCP toolkit
Required to publish in Box Integrations under your own app

prerequisites.title: Box developer account or enterprise access
prerequisites.detail: You need Developer Console access from a Box enterprise or a free developer account. Not every product is on the free plan.

prerequisites.title: Customer admin contact
prerequisites.detail: A customer's Box Admin or Co-Admin needs your app's Client ID to enable it in the Admin Console.

steps.title: Create the Box User app
steps.detail: Log into the Developer Console, select New App, choose User as the app type, and select Create.
steps.done_when: The app exists and shows a Client ID and secret.

steps.title: Get the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Create the Composio auth config for Box with your client ID and secret through Composio's API, then copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: You have the redirect URI from Composio.

steps.title: Register redirect URI and scopes
steps.detail: On the Configuration page, add the HTTPS redirect URI under OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI and set scopes. The redirect must match exactly.
steps.done_when: The URI is saved and the scopes are set.

steps.title: Customer admin enables the app
steps.detail: Give each customer's admin your Client ID. They add it under Platform Apps in the Admin Console.
steps.done_when: The customer can connect the app.

steps.title: Submit the app for listing approval
steps.detail: In the Developer Console choose Apps, then Submit for Approval, and fill out the form.

steps.title: Wait for Box review
steps.detail: Box reviews the listing. No duration is documented.
steps.done_when: The app is approved and listed.

steps.title: Apply to Technology Partner Program
steps.detail: Once the integration is live, complete the application form on Box's partner page.

traps.title: Scope changes need re-authorization
traps.detail: If you change scopes or access level, an admin must re-authorize the app before the changes take effect. Enterprise developers must resubmit it to their admin.

traps.title: Customer admins can block unpublished apps
traps.detail: If a customer turns on 'Disable unpublished apps by default', an admin must explicitly enable your OAuth app.

traps.title: App type cannot be changed
traps.detail: An OAuth 2.0 app cannot be converted to Server Authentication. You would have to create a new app.

traps.title: Short-lived tokens
traps.detail: Access tokens last 60 minutes and refresh tokens 60 days or one use. Long-lived access tokens are not allowed.

traps.title: API calls count against customer allocation
traps.detail: Calls from custom apps count toward the enterprise's monthly allocation, but calls from Box partner integrations do not.

traps.title: Consent screen shows Composio on managed app
traps.detail: With Composio's managed app, users see 'Composio wants to access your account'. Use your own app to show your brand.

blockers.symptom: Customer cannot connect; the app is disabled in their enterprise
blockers.what_it_means: Their admin has not enabled your unpublished OAuth app.
blockers.what_to_do: Send the admin your Client ID and ask them to add it under Platform > Platform Apps.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin instructions with your Client ID.

blockers.what_it_means: With several redirect URIs configured, the authorization URL must include one that matches.
blockers.what_to_do: Include a redirect_uri parameter that exactly matches a configured URI.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the configured URIs against the authorization URL.

evidence.answer: A toolkit appears under 'Composio-managed OAuth available' when Composio manages at least one OAuth method.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method, so each method must be checked on the toolkit's page; this page does not list per-method details for Box.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Open the toolkit page to check each method.
evidence.answer: For Box, the page says to open the toolkit page to check each method.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit.
evidence.answer: Composio can provide the OAuth app that users authorize when they connect a toolkit, so the developer does not need to register an OAuth app or supply a client ID and secret for managed toolkits.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: Developers do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret when Composio provides the app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: If `composio_managed_auth_schemes` contains the toolkit's OAuth method, Composio provides the OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Composio provides the OAuth app when the toolkit's OAuth method is listed in composio_managed_auth_schemes, checked by calling the toolkit endpoint.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: If the field does not contain that method, register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: If the OAuth method is not in composio_managed_auth_schemes, the developer must register their own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: | [Box MCP](/toolkits/box_mcp.md) | `BOX_MCP` |
evidence.answer: The page lists a separate toolkit called Box MCP (slug BOX_MCP) under 'Bring your own OAuth app', which is a different toolkit from Box (BOX) and is not managed by Composio.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: When you use your own OAuth app, you set its authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint on your domain.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect
evidence.answer: The page's example redirect URI is on your own domain at /api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token.
evidence.answer: During OAuth the browser briefly redirects through Composio's backend.composio.dev domain so Composio can capture the auth token.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits also display the Composio backend URL on the consent screen.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
evidence.answer: Proxying the redirect through your own domain is an option if you need to hide Composio's domain.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Add a redirect proxy only when the browser must stay on your domain during the OAuth callback.
evidence.answer: A redirect proxy is only needed when the browser must stay on your domain during the OAuth callback.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately sends a 302 redirect to Composio's callback URL.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**. Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect and must not follow the redirect server-side or fetch Composio itself.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: "Composio wants to access your account" on Google, GitHub, etc.
evidence.answer: By default the consent screen shows 'Composio wants to access your account' on providers such as Google and GitHub; the fix listed is to use your own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: Bringing your own OAuth app is recommended only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: composio_url = "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback"
evidence.answer: The Composio callback endpoint that the proxy forwards to is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see [Managed OAuth apps](/toolkits/managed-auth).
evidence.answer: This page does not mention Box. Its statements below are general, about Composio managed apps for toolkits in general, and do not confirm whether Composio supplies a managed OAuth app for Box.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack. You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains managed OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack (general statement, not Box-specific), so developers do not need to register their own OAuth app for those toolkits.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Managed apps (general, not Box-specific) share their rate-limit quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth (general, not Box-specific) enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval, while a developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With a Composio managed app, end users see a consent screen that says Composio wants to access their account, not the developer's app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.
evidence.answer: A developer can create a custom auth config with their own OAuth app for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances, even when a managed app exists.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Published applications are found in the [Box Integrations][appcenter].
evidence.answer: Platform apps are either published or unpublished. Published apps are listed in Box Integrations.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Box Admins decide whether published and unpublished applications are enabled by default and therefore can be used without approval.
evidence.answer: Box Admins decide whether published and unpublished apps are enabled by default, and so usable without approval.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Regardless of the settings above, in order for an application leveraging JWT or Client Credentials Grant to be used by an enterprise, an Admin must explicitly authorize it via the Box Admin console.
evidence.answer: For apps using JWT or Client Credentials Grant, an enterprise can use the app only after an Admin explicitly authorizes it in the Box Admin console, regardless of the other settings.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If the setting **Disable unpublished apps by default** is turned on, an Admin must also explicitly enable any application leveraging OAuth 2.0 as the authentication method.
evidence.answer: If the 'Disable unpublished apps by default' setting is on, an Admin must also explicitly enable any app using OAuth 2.0.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Additionally, if this setting is turned on, Server Authenticated apps will also require enablement.
evidence.answer: If the 'Disable unpublished apps by default' setting is on, Server Authenticated apps also require enablement.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: They determine which of the 150+ endpoints Access Tokens of an application can successfully call.
evidence.answer: An app's scopes determine which of the 150+ endpoints its Access Tokens can successfully call.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Because scopes work in conjunction with user permissions, granting the write scope does not automatically provide a user with API access to all content in a Box enterprise.
evidence.answer: Scopes work together with user permissions; the write scope does not by itself give access to all enterprise content.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: This is because the read scope is required to perform this action.
evidence.answer: Example from the page: calling a folder-information endpoint requires the read scope, so an app with only manage users and manage groups scopes gets a 403 error for it.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Access Tokens are only valid for 60 minutes, but can be revoked earlier if needed.
evidence.answer: Access Tokens are valid for only 60 minutes, though they can be revoked earlier.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Refresh tokens are valid for 60 days or one use.
evidence.answer: Refresh tokens are valid for 60 days or one use (for OAuth 2.0 apps).

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: For security reasons we do not allow long-lived access tokens.
evidence.answer: Box does not allow long-lived access tokens, for security reasons.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: This means that if a developer revisits the Developer Console and changes the configuration, the Admin must re-authorize the application in order for generated Access Tokens to reflect the changes.
evidence.answer: The authorization is a snapshot: if the developer changes the app configuration in the Developer Console, an Admin must re-authorize the app for new tokens to reflect the changes. This is re-authorization, not a review.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Other endpoints can only be used by an Admin user's Access Token if the enterprise has purchased add-on products such as Box Governance or Box Shield.
evidence.answer: Some endpoints can be used by an Admin's token only if the enterprise has purchased add-on products such as Box Governance or Box Shield.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Creating, deleting, or getting information about users
evidence.answer: Some endpoints, such as creating, deleting, or getting information about users, are restricted to Admins or Co-Admins with the appropriate permissions.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Regardless of the settings above, in order for an application leveraging JWT or Client Credentials Grant to be used by an enterprise, an Admin must explicitly authorize it via the Box Admin console.
evidence.answer: For JWT or Client Credentials apps, an Admin must authorize the app in the Box Admin console before enterprise use.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Upon authorizing one of these applications in the Box Admin Console, a Service Account (`AutomationUser_xxxx_@boxdevedition.com`) representing the application is automatically generated.
evidence.answer: Upon an Admin authorizing a JWT or Client Credentials app, a Service Account representing the app is automatically generated.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Scopes are configured in the [Developer Console][dc] upon application creation.
evidence.answer: Scopes are configured in the Developer Console when the app is created.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Application access is only configured in the [Developer Console][dc] for applications leveraging Server Authentication with JWT or Client Credentials Grant.
evidence.answer: Application access (app access only or app + enterprise access) is set only in the Developer Console, and only for Server Authentication with JWT or Client Credentials Grant apps.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The two options are **app access only** or **app + enterprise access**.
evidence.answer: The two application access options are 'app access only' and 'app + enterprise access'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The Box API follows the same security principles and restrictions as the Box web app. This means that you will not be able to bypass content [permissions][perm], the [waterfall folder structure][waterfall], or Admin-only requirements by leveraging the Box API.
evidence.answer: The Box API does not let apps bypass content permissions, the waterfall folder structure, or Admin-only requirements.
